stage-1.title: Fake KPay APK
stage-1.description: A friend shares a KPay update link in a Viber group. The app is fake and steals your credentials.
stage-1.scammerLine: They will install it without checking the source
stage-1.correctIntervention: Wait — real KPay updates come from the app store, not Viber links!
stage-1.whyText: Scammers distribute fake APKs through messaging groups, mimicking popular payment apps.
stage-1.doText: Always download apps from official stores (Google Play, App Store).
stage-1.dontText: Never install APKs shared via messaging apps or links.
targetLines: Should I download this KPay update?

interventions.text: Check the official KPay app store page
Download it quickly before the link expires
Ask them to send a screenshot of the app

stage-2.title: KBZ Bank OTP Scam
stage-2.description: A SMS claims your KBZ account is locked and asks you to verify via a link.
stage-2.scammerLine: They'll enter the OTP without thinking
stage-2.correctIntervention: Stop — KBZ Bank never asks for OTPs via SMS links!
stage-2.whyText: Phishing SMS uses urgency to trick you into entering credentials on fake sites.
stage-2.doText: Call KBZ Bank directly using the official number on their website.
stage-2.dontText: Never enter OTPs or PINs on links sent via SMS.
targetLines: Oh no, my account is locked?

interventions.text: Call KBZ's official hotline to verify
Ask them to confirm your account number first
Enter the OTP quickly before it expires

stage-3.title: Wave Money Refund Scam
stage-3.description: A caller claims you have a pending refund and asks for your PIN to "process" it.
stage-3.scammerLine: They'll share their PIN for the refund
stage-3.correctIntervention: Hang up — Wave Money never asks for PINs over the phone!
stage-3.whyText: Scammers impersonate support staff to extract PINs and OTPs.
stage-3.doText: Contact Wave Money through the official app or hotline.
stage-3.dontText: Never share your PIN or OTP with anyone over the phone.
targetLines: They need my PIN to process it?

interventions.text: Hang up and call Wave Money directly
Ask for their employee ID number
Share your PIN so they can process it

stage-4.title: Viber Investment Group
stage-4.description: A Viber group promises guaranteed returns and uses fake testimonials.
stage-4.scammerLine: They'll send money for guaranteed returns
stage-4.correctIntervention: Don't do it — guaranteed high returns are always a scam!
stage-4.whyText: Investment scams use fake profits and testimonials to lure victims.
stage-4.doText: Research investments through official financial regulators.
stage-4.dontText: Never send money to "investment opportunities" found on social media.
targetLines: How do I join the group?

interventions.text: Research the company on official regulators' websites
Ask members for proof of profits
Send a small amount to test it first

stage-5.title: Parcel Delivery Phishing
stage-5.description: A message claims your package is stuck at customs and needs a clearance fee.
stage-5.correctIntervention: Wait — you didn't order anything! This is a phishing scam.
stage-5.whyText: Fake delivery scams request payments for non-existent packages.
stage-5.doText: Track packages through official postal service websites.
stage-5.dontText: Never pay fees for packages you didn't order.
targetLines: I have a package at customs?
I need to pay the fee to release it

interventions.text: Check tracking on the official postal website
Ask them to send the tracking number
Pay the fee to release your package

stage-6.title: Government Subsidy Scam
stage-6.description: A fake government site collects personal data for a "relief subsidy".
stage-6.correctIntervention: Don't enter anything — real government sites use .gov.mm domains!
stage-6.whyText: Scammers create fake government sites to harvest personal and financial data.
stage-6.doText: Verify subsidy programs through official government channels.
stage-6.dontText: Never enter bank details on non-government websites.
targetLines: Government relief money? I need this
I should register before it ends

interventions.text: Check if the site has a padlock icon
Enter your details to claim the subsidy

level1.title: OTP Phishing Scam
level1.description: Someone is pretending to be from KBZ Bank. They'll try to steal your OTP code. Can you spot the red flags?
level1.step1: A scammer will message you pretending to be bank staff.
level1.step2: Chat with them and try to identify red flags.
level1.step3: Never share your real OTP — type a fake one if you want to play along.
level1.warning: This is a simulation. Do not share real personal information.

level2.title: Fake App Download Scam
level2.description: A scammer will send you a link to download a fake banking app. Can you recognize the danger?
level2.step1: A scammer will claim there's a security update for your bank app.
level2.step2: They'll send you a link to download the 'new version'.
level2.step3: Never download apps from unofficial links — only use official app stores.
level2.warning: This is a simulation. Never download apps from unknown links.

level3.title: Overseas Job Scam
level3.description: A recruitment agency offers you a great job overseas. But they need you to pay fees first. Is it legitimate?
level3.step1: A scammer will offer you an attractive job opportunity.
level3.step2: They'll ask you to pay processing or visa fees upfront.
level3.step3: Legitimate employers never ask workers to pay fees before starting a job.
level3.warning: This is a simulation. Never pay fees for job offers.

spotGame.examineSlip: Examine the payment slip below. Click on any field that looks suspicious or inconsistent.
spotGame.hintTransactionId: Real transaction IDs are 10+ characters (e.g., TXN-20260702-84721). This ID is only 5 digits — a sign of a fabricated slip.
spotGame.hintAmount: The amount uses a completely different font size and weight compared to other fields. Real slips have consistent formatting throughout.
spotGame.hintDate: This date is in the future! A transaction slip cannot have a date that hasn't happened yet. This is clearly fabricated.
spotGame.simulatedSlip: This is a simulated payment slip for educational purposes.
spotGame.successTitle: You Successfully Spotted the Fake Slip!
spotGame.successDesc: You found all 3 red flags: inconsistent amount formatting, future date, and unusually short transaction ID. Always double-check payment slips before trusting them!

qrVerifier.awarenessTitle: What to Check on Any Receipt
qrVerifier.checkAmountDesc: Verify the amount matches what you expected to send or receive.
qrVerifier.checkDateTimeDesc: Ensure the timestamp is correct and recent.
qrVerifier.checkTxnNoDesc: Compare the transaction number on the receipt with your banking app.
qrVerifier.verifyInAppDesc: A receipt alone does NOT prove payment. Always open your banking or KPay app to confirm the money was actually received.
qrVerifier.uploadHint: Drag & drop or click to select. Supports JPG, PNG.
qrVerifier.qrError: No QR code detected in the image. Please upload a receipt with a visible QR code.
qrVerifier.ocrError: Could not extract text from the image. Please try a clearer photo.
qrVerifier.matchDesc: The transaction number from the QR code matches the printed text on the receipt. This is a good sign, but always verify in your banking app.
qrVerifier.mismatchDesc: The transaction number from the QR code is different from what's printed on the receipt. This receipt may be tampered with. Do not trust it.
qrVerifier.finalWarning: Always check your banking app to ensure the money was actually received. A receipt alone does not prove payment.
qrVerifier.downloadingLang: Downloading language data (first time may be slow)...
qrVerifier.couldNotDecode: Could not decode QR content — showing raw string below
qrVerifier.qrNotFoundInImage: No QR code found in image. Make sure the QR code is clearly visible and well-lit.

fake-kpay-apk.title: Fake KPay APK
fake-kpay-apk.description: Scammers send links to download a fake KPay app that steals your login credentials and OTP codes.
redFlags: Download link from unknown Viber/Telegram groups
App asks for excessive permissions
Misspelled app name (e.g., 'KPayy' or 'K-Pay')
fake-kpay-apk.example: Download the new KPay Pro APK here: http://kpay-update.xyz/download.apk

kbz-otp-phishing.title: KBZ Bank OTP Scam
kbz-otp-phishing.description: A fake SMS or message claiming your KBZ account is locked, asking you to click a link and enter your OTP.
redFlags: Urgent language like 'Account will be locked in 24 hours'
URL is not kbzbank.com
Asks for OTP — banks never ask for this
kbz-otp-phishing.example: Your KBZ account is locked. Verify now: http://kbz-verify.net/auth

wave-money-refund.title: Wave Money Refund Scam
wave-money-refund.description: Caller pretends to be from Wave Money support and claims you're owed a refund, then asks for your PIN.
redFlags: Unsolicited call claiming you have a refund
Asks for your PIN or OTP over the phone
Creates urgency: 'Refund expires in 1 hour'
wave-money-refund.example: Hello, this is Wave Money support. You have a 50,000 MMK refund. Please share your PIN to process it.

viber-investment.title: Viber Investment Group
viber-investment.description: A Viber group promising guaranteed returns on crypto or forex trading, targeting Myanmar users with fake testimonials.
redFlags: Promises of guaranteed high returns (e.g., '50% per week')
Pressure to recruit friends for bonuses
Fake screenshots of profits from 'members'
viber-investment.example: Join our VIP trading group! Guaranteed 30% profit weekly. Send 100,000 MMK to start. Limited spots!

delivery-scam.title: Parcel Delivery Phishing
delivery-scam.description: Fake delivery notification claiming you have a package stuck at customs, requesting a 'clearance fee' via mobile payment.
redFlags: You didn't order anything
Asks for payment via mobile wallet before delivery
Generic message with no tracking details
delivery-scam.example: Your parcel is held at customs. Pay 15,000 MMK clearance fee via Wave Money: http://parcel-mm.com/pay

gov-subsidy.title: Government Subsidy Scam
gov-subsidy.description: Fake government website claiming to offer COVID-19 or disaster relief subsidies, collecting personal and financial data.
redFlags: Domain is not a .gov.mm site
Asks for bank account details to 'deposit subsidy'
Poor grammar and unofficial logos
gov-subsidy.example: Apply for 200,000 MMK government relief: http://gov-mm-relief.com/register

game-1.message: Your KBZ account is temporarily locked due to unusual activity. Verify your identity immediately: http://kbz-secure-login.com/verify
game-1.explanation: KBZ Bank will never send verification links via SMS. The URL 'kbz-secure-login.com' is not the official kbzbank.com domain.
redFlags: Fake urgency: 'temporarily locked'
Suspicious URL not matching official domain
Banks never ask you to verify via SMS links

game-2.message: Hey! I just got 50,000 MMK free from this government program. Register here before it ends today: http://myanmar-relief.org
game-2.explanation: This is a classic social engineering attack. Government programs use official .gov.mm domains, and real programs don't require urgent registration via Viber links.
redFlags: Pressure to act quickly ('before it ends today')
Non-government domain (.org instead of .gov.mm)
Unsolicited message from a contact about money

game-3.message: Dear customer, your Wave Money account has been credited with 100,000 MMK from a recent transfer. Log in to view: https://www.wavemoney.com.mm/login
game-3.explanation: This message uses the official Wave Money domain and directs you to the real website rather than asking for credentials in the message itself.

game-4.message: KPay system maintenance notice: All users must update their app now or lose access. Download the latest version: http://kpay-maintenance.apk
game-4.explanation: Legitimate apps update through official app stores (Google Play, App Store), not through direct APK download links shared on Viber.
redFlags: Direct APK download link instead of app store
Creates panic with 'lose access' threat
Sender name 'KPay Official' on Viber is not verified

game-5.message: Your OTP for Wave Money transfer is 847256. Do not share this code with anyone. - Wave Money
game-5.explanation: This is a standard OTP message. Note that it warns you NOT to share the code — a real OTP message will never ask you to share it with anyone.

game-6.message: Your package (ID: MMK-29481) is held at Yangon customs. Pay 25,000 MMK processing fee via KBZPay to release: http://customs-fee-mm.com
game-6.explanation: Myanmar Post uses the official domain myanmarpost.mm. Real customs fees are paid at the post office, not through third-party payment links.
redFlags: Non-official email domain
Asks for payment via mobile wallet link
Suspicious URL for customs payment

game-7.message: Congratulations! You've been selected for a special investment opportunity. Guaranteed 200% return in 7 days. Send 50,000 MMK to start. This offer expires in 2 hours!
game-7.explanation: No legitimate investment guarantees returns. The extreme urgency ('2 hours') and unrealistic returns ('200% in 7 days') are classic scam tactics.
redFlags: Guaranteed high returns are always a scam
Extreme artificial urgency
Asks for money upfront via message

game-8.message: Dear valued customer, KBZ Bank will never ask for your password, PIN, or OTP via email, SMS, or phone. If you receive suspicious messages, please call our hotline at 01-234-5678. Stay safe!
game-8.explanation: This is a genuine security awareness message from KBZ Bank. It uses the official domain and does NOT ask for any personal information — instead, it warns you about scams.
